**Weekly “Stay‑Home‑Ready” Action Plan** Below is a concise, step‑by‑step checklist you can complete this week so that you’ll have a self‑sufficient kitchen for several days without grocery runs or deliveries. All steps are drawn from the emergency‑pantry system and the minimalist core‑staples plan already captured in the wiki [[summaries/session‑14_2024‑06‑01]], [[summaries/session‑40_2025‑06‑01]], and the related concepts. | Day / Phase | What to Do | Why it Helps | |-------------|------------|--------------| | **Day 1 – Quick Inventory** | 1. Open every pantry, fridge, and freezer shelf.
2. Write down each item and its expiry (month & year).
3. Highlight anything **missing** from the Core Staples list (rice, pasta, canned beans, olive oil, vinegar, salt, pepper, a couple of spices, tomato paste/canned tomatoes, eggs, cheese, lemons/limes, onions, garlic, frozen veg, frozen berries, a backup protein such as shrimp or chicken‑thighs). | Gives you a baseline to know exactly what you have and what you need for a few‑day buffer. | | **Day 1 – FIFO Check** | Apply the **FIFO rotation** rule (oldest items at the front/left, newest at the back/right) and label each item with its month‑year if not already labeled (see [[concepts/fifo‑rotation]]). | Guarantees you’ll use the oldest food first, preventing waste and keeping your emergency stash fresh. | | **Day 2 – Restock Core Staples** | 1. Make a short shopping list for any missing core staples (buy only the quantities you’ll need ≈ 1 week).
2. Purchase **1–2 proteins** (e.g., chicken‑thighs and/or frozen shrimp) and a handful of versatile fresh veg (broccoli, bell peppers, mixed greens).
3. Grab any missing pantry basics (rice, pasta, canned beans, olive oil, vinegar, tomato paste). | The **Core Staples** concept is designed to let you create many meals from a tiny, interchangeable inventory, so a small, focused shop is enough. | | **Day 2 – Label & Store** | As you bring items home, immediately label them with month‑year and place them in the correct **shelf zone** (everyday staples eye‑level, heavy bulk low, backups high) [[concepts/pantry‑shelf‑zoning]]. | Keeps the pantry organized and makes future FIFO pulls effortless. | | **Day 3 – Meal‑Plan & Prep** | 1. Sketch a **1‑week meal flow** using the template from Session 40 (e.g., protein‑rice bowl → pasta → stir‑fry → egg‑based skillet, etc.).
2. Cook a modest batch of **rice** and **pasta** (enough for two meals each). Store in airtight containers. | Pre‑cooked grains act as the backbone for lunches and quick dinners, minimizing daily cooking time when you’re confined. | | **Day 3 – Leftover Strategy** | Plan each dinner to generate a lunch‑ready portion for the next day (e.g., roast chicken → next‑day rice bowl). | Guarantees you have ready‑to‑eat meals with minimal extra prep. | | **Day 4 – Emergency Checklist** | Fill out the **Restock‑Routine checklist** (quarterly review) with today’s date:
• Verify all core staples are stocked ≥ 3 days supply.
• Move any items ≤ 6 months to the front for priority use.
• Note any items to buy next restock. | The checklist from Session 14 creates a repeatable habit so you stay prepared long‑term. | | **Day 5 – “Mystery‑Item” Decision Tree** | Inspect any canned goods or bottled water without dates. Use the decision tree (safe‑use vs. discard) to either label with today’s date or set aside for disposal. | Prevents you from unknowingly relying on unsafe food during a lockdown. | | **Day 6 – Quick Test Run** | Prepare a **full‑day** menu using only core staples and the fresh items you bought (e.g., breakfast omelet, lunch rice‑chicken bowl, dinner pasta‑veg). Track any missing ingredient. | Reveals gaps in your stash before a real emergency occurs. | | **Day 7 – Final Review** | Verify that:
• All core staples are present and labeled.
• Meals for the next 3‑5 days can be assembled from existing inventory.
• You have a printed or digital copy of the **Restock Routine** and **FIFO** guidelines on the fridge door. | Gives you peace of mind that you’re truly covered. | --- ### Quick Reference: Core Staples Checklist | Category | Items (minimum) | |----------|-----------------| | **Pantry** | Rice, pasta, canned beans, olive oil, vinegar, salt, pepper, 1–2 spices, tomato paste or canned tomatoes | | **Fridge** | Eggs, block cheese, lemons/limes, onions, garlic | | **Freezer** | Mixed frozen veg, frozen berries, shrimp **or** chicken‑thighs (backup protein) | *(All items are listed as **product** entities in the wiki: [[entities/rice]], [[entities/pasta]], [[entities/olive‑oil]], [[entities/shrimp]], [[entities/chicken‑thighs]], etc.)* --- ### Why This Works 1. **Minimal, versatile inventory** → You can mix‑and‑match to create a variety of meals without needing a long shopping list. 2. **FIFO & labeling** → Freshness is assured, and you’ll never waste a can because you can’t see its date. 3. **Structured restock routine** → A single weekly “maintenance” window prevents last‑minute panic and keeps the emergency pantry ready. 4. **Leftover‑first meal flow** → Every dinner produces a lunch, cutting daily cooking time when you’re stuck at home. Follow the above week‑long plan, and you’ll be equipped with enough food, organized storage, and a proven routine to comfortably weather several days without external supplies. Stay safe and well‑fed!
